whatItDoes: Computes the equated monthly installment (EMI) for a fixed-rate loan, plus the total payment and the total interest you will pay over the full term. Uses a standard reducing-balance EMI formula.
whyItExists: Understanding a loan's full cost is the difference between an affordable purchase and a debt trap. An EMI calculator reveals not just the monthly payment but how much interest compounds over the whole loan life.
whoShouldUse: Home buyers, car buyers, personal-loan borrowers, and financial planners estimating loan affordability.
useCases: Estimate the monthly payment of a home, car, or personal loan
Compare loan terms of different durations and rates
See the total interest paid over the life of a loan
Budget a repayment plan that fits your cash flow
instructions: Enter the annual interest rate in percent
Read the monthly EMI, total payment, and total interest
Experiment with shorter terms to see how interest shrinks
bestPractices: Compare the total interest, not just the monthly EMIs
Try shorter tenures to reduce total interest when you can afford it
Include points, fees, and insurance burden separately
Re-check the rate with the lender, since rates change all the time
commonMistakes: Comparing loans only on their interest rates, ignoring tenure
Entering the rate as 0.085 instead of 8.5
Forgetting that processing fees and insurance are not in the EMI
Assuming the EMI amount stays constant forever on a variable-rate loan
faq: What is the EMI formula? — It is the standard reducing-balance annuity: principal × monthly rate × (1+rate)^n / ((1+rate)^n − 1).
Does it include processing fees or insurance? — No, only principal and interest.
Can I use it for any loan type? — Yes, the math is identical for home, auto, and personal loans.
Is my data sent anywhere? — No, the calculation happens entirely in your browser.
features: Adjustable loan amount, rate, and tenure
